title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of filament light sources and LED replacement light sources for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and of their trailers
scope_summary: R37 approves types of standardised filament (incandescent, including halogen) light sources and their LED replacement light sources (LEDr) belonging to the categories listed in Annex 1. These light sources are intended for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and their trailers.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to filament light sources and their LED replacement light sources shown in Annex 1 and intended for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and of their trailers.
vehicle_categories: Power-driven vehicles (categories not restricted, e.g. L, M, N, T)
applies_to_components: Filament light sources (incandescent technology), including halogen filament light sources
Filament light sources emitting white, selective-yellow, amber or red light (coloured or coated bulbs)
LED replacement light sources (LEDr) of standardised categories
AE devices (Additional Electronics devices) supplied with LED replacement light sources
Light source caps (IEC 60061), including oversize caps of LEDr
Packaging and instructions of LED replacement light sources
relation_to_other_regulations: Definitions of Resolution R.E.5 (incl. AE device) apply (para. 2.1); filament/LEDr category data sheets, lists and groups are given in Annex 1, which since 22.06.2017 refers to the consolidated light source category sheets in the Resolution
Technical definitions of Resolution R.E.4 (common specification of light source categories) apply (para. 3.1)
Colour definitions of UN Regulation No. 48 apply (paras. 3.3.3.2, 3.4.5.1)
LED replacement light sources must meet the ESA requirements of UN Regulation No. 10 (EMC) (para. 3.4.7.3)
Optical quality of filament light sources with internal shield is checked in a standard headlamp against the passing-beam requirements of 'the relevant' headlamp Regulation (para. 3.3.6)
Caps must comply with IEC Publication 60061 cap data sheets; signalling filament light sources must meet para. 4.4.2 of IEC 60809 Ed. 3
Distinguishing numbers of Contracting Parties per R.E.3; approval number per 1958 Agreement Rev.3 Schedule 4
Light sources are for use in lamps approved under the respective lamp regulations; installation on vehicles is governed by the installation regulations (e.g. R48), not R37

defined_terms.label: Light source category
defined_terms.definition: Different basic design of standardised filament light sources (incandescent) or LED replacement light sources (LED technology), each with a specific designation such as H4, P21W, T4W, PY21W or RR10W.

defined_terms.label: LEDr category
defined_terms.definition: A distinct category bearing the same designation as its counterpart filament light source category, designed to replace it with equivalent performance using LED technology, described in a separate data sheet in Annex 1.

defined_terms.label: Filament light source type
defined_terms.definition: Filament light sources within the same category differing in trade name/mark, bulb and/or cap design affecting optical results, rated voltage, or halogen.

defined_terms.label: LEDr type
defined_terms.definition: LED replacement light sources within the same category differing in trade name/mark, light source design affecting optical results, rated voltage, high-efficiency, particular electrical polarity, or oversize cap.

defined_terms.label: Filament light source
defined_terms.definition: Light source in which the filament(s) are the only element(s) that generate and emit light when energized.

defined_terms.label: LEDr
defined_terms.definition: Light source in which solid-state junction(s), possibly with fluorescence-based conversion elements, are the only elements generating light, replacing a counterpart filament light source category; marked 'LEDr'.

defined_terms.label: High-efficiency LEDr
defined_terms.definition: LEDr whose electrical current at test voltage is below the objective minimum current of the data sheet (without or with disconnected AE device), marked with the character 'ͰE'.

defined_terms.label: Additional Electronics device
defined_terms.definition: Optional additional electronics device (as defined in R.E.5) supplied for listed vehicle applications of an LEDr, bearing a specific identification code starting with 'Æ'.

defined_terms.label: AE device identification code
defined_terms.definition: Code of an AE device comprising 'Æ', the approval country number and the approval code of the LEDr with which it has been approved.

defined_terms.label: Polarity-dependent LEDr
defined_terms.definition: LEDr that operates in only one electrical position, to be marked '+'/'―' at the terminals if it can be inserted in more than one position.

defined_terms.label: Oversize cap
defined_terms.definition: LEDr cap whose dimensions not relevant for interchangeability exceed the IEC 60061 cap sheet within maximum deviations allowed in the category data sheet.

defined_terms.label: Halogen / UV-compliant ('U')
defined_terms.definition: Halogen filament light source subject to the UV radiation limit of para. 3.3.4 and marked 'U' when complying.

defined_terms.label: Selective-yellow
defined_terms.definition: Filament light source with a selective-yellow bulb or outer bulb solely changing the colour of a white-light source, which does not constitute a change of type.

defined_terms.label: Dual-filament
defined_terms.definition: Filament light source with two filaments (high/low wattage), each aged and assessed separately.

defined_terms.label: Line filament
defined_terms.definition: Filament whose length is determined by the apices of its first and last turns, measured parallel (axial) or perpendicular (transverse) to the reference axis.

defined_terms.label: Étalon light source
defined_terms.definition: Filament light source with additional tighter requirements per Annex 1 data sheets, used for photometric testing of lamps.

defined_terms.label: Standard headlamp
defined_terms.definition: Approved headlamp of effective diameter ≥160 mm which with a standard filament light source gives ≤90 % of maximum and ≥120 % of minimum limits, used for optical quality checks.

defined_terms.label: Low UV LEDr
defined_terms.definition: LED replacement light source whose weighted UV radiation complies with the kUV limit of para. 3.4.6.

applicability_hints: Applies only to light sources of categories listed in Annex 1 (via the R.E. category sheets); light sources of other categories or technologies (e.g. gas-discharge, LED light sources of their own categories, non-replaceable sources) are not covered here.
Covers both headlamp/front-lighting bulbs (e.g. H1, H4, H7, H11) and signalling bulbs (e.g. P21W, PY21W, W5W, T4W, R10W), including small wedge/festoon bulbs.

An aftermarket LED retrofit bulb can only be approved under R37 as an 'LEDr' if an LED replacement category data sheet exists for that designation; it must be of the same cap designation and meet the counterpart's performance.
LED replacement light sources are themselves ESAs and must meet UN R10 EMC requirements.
Adapters, CANbus decoders or load modules supplied with LEDr fall under R37 as AE devices and must be marked with an 'Æ' identification code tied to the LEDr approval.
Packaging and consumer instructions (website vehicle-applicability listing, warnings) of LEDr are regulated, not just the product.
A selective-yellow bulb or outer bulb on an otherwise white filament source is not a new type and may share the same approval code.
Standard (étalon) filament light sources used by labs to test lamps also fall under R37 with additional requirements.
Coated/coloured bulbs (amber, red, selective-yellow) are covered, with a solvent-wipe test for coated bulbs.
The regulation approves the light source as a component; its use in a lamp is governed by the lamp approval and vehicle installation regulations.
